newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel profits fell 68 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel profits fell 68 percent.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp. Wednesday said its profits fell 68 percent in the third quarter and announced it will sell or close operations that employ more than 1,900 people.

The nation's second-biggest steelmaker said it will take a $375 million charge in the current quarter to pay for the new restructuring plan. Falling prices and shipments and a previously announced restructuring charge hurt third-quarter results, it said.

The Bethlehem, Pa.-based company said net income fell to $11 million in the quarter from $34 million in the 1995 quarter. Earnings per share were nil vs. 22 cents. Sales fell 4 percent to $1.17 billion from $1.22 billion.
Excluding the third quarter's $15 million restructuring charge, earnings would have been $23 million, or 12 cents a share.

Bethlehem also said it plans to sell Bethlehem Structural Products, which makes steel shapes and piling, BethForge, a maker of forged steel products, Centec Roll Corp., which produces steel rolls for metal-working, and a ship repair yard in Sparrows Point, Md. The other operations are all in Bethlehem.

The businesses together employ about 1,935 people and generate less than 10 percent of total revenues, Bethlehem said. It will shut the operations if buyers cannot be found and continue efforts to sell them whole or piecemeal.
"These businesses ... have continued to be unprofitable, even with our efforts to modernise and improve them," Chairman Curtis Barnette said in a statement.
Employees affected will receive any benefits they are entitled to, training and outplacement assistance, the company said.
In addition, Bethlehem said it write off a coke producing unit as an impaired asset, though the business will continue operating. Coke is used in steelmaking.
Bethlehem stock added 12.5 cents to $8.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
